selection: Deliberate: finite reconstruction programs and paid encoder selection, after aligned-history validation failed its randomized control and the prior calibration audit supported keeping SSE.
hypothesis: The compact encoder's repeated current literal-event charge differs from the exact adaptive cost of the same literal sequence, even with unchanged decoded-context keys. An encoder-only cost helper can reproduce the actual token model's conditional costs without mutating decoder state.
source_finding: compress_inner uses L*tok.evc(st,0) for candidate literal spans. TOK.eve updates CM counts after every emitted event, and its context is (st.f,st.w,st.pg,st.c). Existing literal predictions and updates also run for every copied byte.
deliverable: One bounded cost helper plus tests against the authenticated original CM implementation, including an exact rational counterexample, repeated and interleaved contexts, rescaling, and nonmutation.
mechanism: For a proposed all-literal span, copy only the relevant event-count triples, compute each zero-event conditional probability, then perform the original count increment and4096-total rescaling on the local copies. Return cumulative costs, leaving the authoritative models untouched.
stop_rule: Any mismatch with sequential original CM probabilities or any authoritative-state mutation blocks integration. Passing demonstrates cost accounting only; a separately frozen P/K/D exact archive comparison is required before claiming compression benefit.
non_goals: No entropy coder, predictor, SSE, history bank, decoder or corpus mutation.
No claimed global optimal parse or finite archive gain from ideal event-cost differences.
No1MB continuation of the rejected field-history configuration, and no selection of its randomized control.
No installation, model download, HORIZON or MIDAS change.
